DeHxxpCmWEu.caption:
Which attachment style resonates most for you??!👀

Understanding your attachment style can FINALLY help you understand what happens inside you when connection feels shaky, conflict hits, or you’re scared of losing someone you love.

Like… Do you chase reassurance?? Shut down? Pull away?? Panic when someone feels distant, then feel trapped when they get too close?

I loooove talking attachment styles as a therapist, because once you recognize your pattern, you can start catching it before it runs the whole damn relationship.

Bottom line?? Your attachment style may help explain the protective moves you learned - but it does not have to dictate what you do next. And THAT is where the real work starts: Noticing the fear underneath the reaction, communicating what you actually need, taking accountability for the impact, and practicing a different response little by little.

Comment POD to get this week’s After Bedtime ep that walks through this - AND how to work on addressing core attachment wound stuff - right to youuu 🤸‍♂️

So… which one hit a little too close to home? 👀 Secure, anxious, avoidant, or fearful-avoidant?? (The good news: With some intentional work, you can totally reshape your attachment style and build towards ✨earned secure attachment✨ aka the deep work that sooo many of us here in the BLF bestie crew are doing daily, with ourselves, our partners, our kids).

DeIDQsODAis.caption:
Raise your hand if your Monday started with "I DON'T WANT TO GO TO SCHOOL!" 🙋‍♀️

Can we be honest for a second? Some Mondays, I don't want to go either. Most of us wake up with our own version of that feeling, we've just learned to keep it inside. So when our kid says it out loud, it makes sense that it gets to us.

If tomorrow morning brings more of the same, try this: before you say anything else, just agree with the feeling. Then let me know how it goes.

Dcq2baejOXf.caption:
Your kid can be furious with you and still be safe with you. Just like how you can be annoyed at the pilot, but trust that you're safe on the plane. Those two things happen at the same time more often than we think.

Holding a boundary while your kid is upset with you is one of the hardest parts of this job. It's uncomfortable and it's normal to want to cave just to make the noise stop. That urge doesn't mean you're weak, it means you love your kid and you don't like seeing them upset.

But here's the thing. Your kid's protest is not proof you're doing something wrong. Sometimes it's proof you're doing something right, and they just don't have the words for relief yet, only the words for frustration.

You don't need your kid's approval to know you're a good parent. You need your own sturdiness. Next time you set a boundary you believe in and your child protests? Hold steady. You’re the pilot of your family’s plane. And we’re honored to be your co-pilot, every great pilot has one. 💛

Ddy2lyDF6Q1.caption:
Your child throws cards everywhere when they lose at Uno... storms off the baseball field when the other team wins... won't participate unless they're guaranteed a win.

In these moments, something unmanageable is happening in their body. For a lot of kids, losing brings up feelings of not being good enough, and the big reaction on the surface is a response to that feeling, not to the loss itself.

Part of what makes this all so uncomfortable is watching your kid feel something you can't fix for them. You want to hand them a reason it's okay, a stat, a silver lining, anything that gets them back to feeling good fast. But confidence isn't built in the fast recovery. It's built in the quiet, in a kid learning they can feel disappointed and still be completely fine.

Losing well isn't a character trait some kids have and others don't. It's a confidence skill, and it's one we can actually teach. If this resonates, learn more about confidence and Good Inside at the link in my bio.

Spring gets all the glory for cleaning and resetting. But I’ll say it: fall is my favorite time to deal with toys.
 
Kids are back in school. Routines have settled down. The house is quiet again for a few hours. And after a summer of nonstop play, there’s finally room - and time - to see what’s actually in there.

Here’s a few more tips:

I’ve made plenty of mistakes with toy storage over the years, but here’s what I’ve learned:

* Toys need to be seen. Out of sight = out of mind.

* Lose the boxes. Packaging wastes space and hides what’s inside.

* Keep choices manageable. Too many options overwhelm kids. Fewer toys = easier decisions = more play.

* Give toys a home. A designated spot for each toy is a game changer - and makes clean-up easier for everyone. 

Just promise me you’ll remember one thing as you head into organization mode: Toys aren’t junk. 

They’re the tools kids use to play, imagine, explore, and learn - so a little care in how you handle them goes a long way 😉 

Think how you’d feel if someone call all your most beloved treasures trash or clutter. It’s important to be kind, as always. 

Comment STORAGE for links to these and more organization ideas.

דפדפו ותראו למה אני מתכוונת:
✨ערכת הגלגל: הם פשוט לא מפסיקים לבקש לשחק בזה שוב ושוב. חבר’ה, רחמו על הגננת, בא לי לגוון! 😂
✨ערכת פשוט אלף-בית: חפרו לי שגיל 3 זה מוקדם מדי.שומו שמיים, צדקתם! עכשיו הם משחקים בזה בכיף ונחשפים לצלילים, ואני מתחרטת כי בניתי על קצת שקט... ✨לומדים לגזור: מאז שהיא בגן הם רוצים רק לגזור ולגזור. מי בא לטאטא פה את הרצפה? 🤪🧹
✨המשחק המחיק: עפים על זה שזה מחיק. לא אכפת להם לטעות, הם פשוט מוחקים ומנסים שוב. מאיפה הביטחון העצמי המוגזם הזה?! 
✨מזהים צבעים בכיף: הם כבר מזמן יודעים את כל הצבעים והצורות בעל פה, ועדיין מסרבים לשחרר את הערכה. ניצחתם את המשחק, שחררו! 🏆
✨לומדים ומשחקים בכיף: כמה אפשר לשחק במפגש? מתישהו צריך ללמוד ברצינות! מה זה הרוגע והכיף הזה בזמן הלמידה?! 🤷‍♀️
✨מעברים בכיף: הערכה שהרסה לי את הגן!!!
בא לי קצת בלאגן וצעקות במעברים, והרוגע והשקט הנעים הזה פשוט מטריד!🤫

🎯 והשורה התחתונה?
הילדים מרותקים, הלמידה קורית מעצמה, ואני? אני כנראה אמשיך “לסבול” מהשקט וההנאה שלהם❤️
איזו ערכה חסרה לכם בגן או בבית כדי שתוכלו “להתחרט” עליה גם? 
ספרו לי בתגובות או שלחו לי הודעה פרטית ואשלח לכם קישור לערכות השוות האלה👇✨
